 Frequently Asked Questions 
 48V 65Ah LiMAX Golf Cart Battery FAQs
 Common questions about fitment, range, charging, installation, and monitoring.
 Will this battery fit my specific golf cart? 
 The Epoch 48V 65Ah LiMAX kit is configured for Club Car Precedent, EZGO RXV, EZGO TXT, Yamaha 2007–2010, Yamaha 2011+, and Other (ICON and other compatible 48V carts). It is not a drop-in replacement for every installation: confirm that the battery bay fits the 17.20 × 14.33 × 7.48 in case, and check terminal clearance, cable routing, charge-port wiring, the On-Board Computer (OBC) on Club Car Precedent carts, and that your controller’s current demand fits the battery ratings before installation.
 Do I need to buy a separate lithium charger? 
 No. This is a complete kit and includes a 48V 10A onboard lithium charger with a 10 ft heavy-duty extension cord, along with a digital battery gauge, a remote on/off switch with wiring harness, a 12V converter, a cart-specific charge port plug, and mounting brackets. Do not use an old lead-acid charger unless it is confirmed and programmed for LiFePO4 charging, with equalization and desulfation modes disabled.
 How long does it take to charge, and how do I plug in? 
 About 6.5 hours from empty with the included 48V 10A onboard lithium charger. The charger is powered through the cart’s charge port: the kit’s cart-specific charge port plug replaces the factory lead-acid receptacle (replacing it is required for safety), and the included 10 ft heavy-duty extension cord connects the charge port to a standard 120V outlet. If the charger stays connected, it restarts charging when the state of charge drops below about 95%.
 Can I charge the battery in freezing weather? 
 No. This battery has no internal heater, and the BMS blocks charging outside 0°C to 55°C (32°F to 131°F), so let a cold battery warm above freezing before charging. It can discharge from -10°C to 55°C (14°F to 131°F).
 What is the estimated range of the 48V 65Ah battery? 
 Range depends on cart weight, passengers, terrain, tire size, controller settings, and driving style. Epoch estimates approximately 25 to 35 miles per charge for stock or mildly upgraded carts under normal conditions. For more range, two matched batteries can be connected in parallel for a 48V, 130Ah system.
 Will a lithium battery make my golf cart go faster? 
 In many carts, switching from a heavy lead-acid bank to a lighter lithium battery improves acceleration, hill-climbing response, handling, and braking feel. Top speed still depends on your motor, controller, tires, programming, and local cart settings, but the weight savings and flat LiFePO4 voltage curve help the cart feel stronger throughout the discharge cycle.
 Do I need to bypass the On-Board Computer on my Club Car? 
 Some older Club Car models that use an On-Board Computer to manage the original lead-acid charger may require an OBC bypass when converting to lithium. This is a common part of many Club Car lithium conversions and allows the included Epoch lithium charger to charge the battery directly. Confirm the correct procedure for your exact model year before installation.
 Is the 65Ah battery large enough for an upgraded motor or Navitas controller? 
 The 65Ah LiMAX kit is a strong choice for stock carts and mild upgrades: the battery is rated for 200A maximum continuous discharge, with 300A for up to 15 seconds and 700A for up to 2 seconds for acceleration. Heavily modified carts with high-amp aftermarket controllers, aggressive motor upgrades, oversized tires, or steep hill use may require a larger-capacity LiMAX kit with higher sustained output headroom.
 How do I know how much battery life I have left? 
 The kit includes a digital Bluetooth battery gauge for the dash, which shows state of charge from 0 to 100%, voltage, current, temperature, and warnings. The free Epoch Li-Ion app for iOS and Android shows the same readings plus cycle data and battery health on your phone.
 Can I connect two 48V 65Ah LiMAX batteries together? 
 Yes, in parallel only. Epoch lists this model for up to two batteries in parallel, which create a 48V 130Ah system for extended range. Use matched BB5165A-Kit-1 batteries of similar age, condition, and firmware, charged to the same state of charge, and install them according to Epoch’s configuration guidance. Do not connect them in series.

 Will This ICON Lithium Battery Fit My 48V ICON Golf Cart?
 Will This ICON Lithium Battery Fit My 48V ICON Golf Cart?
 Yes. This Vatrer ICON lithium battery is designed for 48V ICON golf carts and replaces the existing AGM, gel, or lead-acid battery bank with a single 105Ah LiFePO4 battery. 
 Can It Replace the Original 6-Battery Setup in My ICON?
 Can It Replace the Original 6-Battery Setup in My ICON?
 Yes. Many 48V ICON golf carts use a multi-battery AGM, gel, or lead-acid setup, and this kit converts that arrangement to one 48V 105Ah lithium golf cart battery. Removing the multi-battery bank also reduces the number of inter-battery cables and connections that need to be maintained after the conversion.
 Can I Keep Using My Original ICON Charger?
 Can I Keep Using My Original ICON Charger?
 Use the included 58.4V 18A LiFePO4 charger instead of a charger configured for AGM, gel, or flooded lead-acid batteries. The lithium charger uses the charging profile required by this battery, so replacing the original lead-acid charger is an important part of the ICON golf cart battery replacement.
 Will My Original ICON Battery Gauge Still Show the Correct Charge Level?
 Will My Original ICON Battery Gauge Still Show the Correct Charge Level?
 A voltage-based factory gauge may not provide an accurate SOC reading after a lithium conversion because LiFePO4 voltage remains relatively stable through much of the discharge cycle. Use the included LCD or Bluetooth monitoring instead; both give you battery data directly from the lithium system and provide a more useful indication of remaining charge.
 Why Would My ICON Power On but Not Drive After a Lithium Conversion?
 Why Would My ICON Power On but Not Drive After a Lithium Conversion?
 Some ICON configurations use the original charger circuit as a drive interlock, preventing the cart from moving while charging. If the cart powers up after installation but will not drive, the charger-interlock circuit is one of the first items to check rather than assuming the new battery has failed. The interlock needs to remain correctly configured when the original charging setup is replaced.
 Will My ICON Lights and USB Ports Still Work with the Lithium Battery?
 Will My ICON Lights and USB Ports Still Work with the Lithium Battery?
 Yes, when the cart's 12V accessories remain connected through the proper DC-DC conversion circuit. Lights, USB ports, radios, and other 12V accessories should not be connected directly to the 48V battery; keep them on the factory voltage reducer or use a suitable 48V-to-12V reducer where required.
 Is 105Ah Enough for an ICON i40 or i60 Used with Passengers?
 Is 105Ah Enough for an ICON i40 or i60 Used with Passengers?
 The 105Ah configuration is aimed at regular golf, neighborhood transportation, and passenger use without moving up to the larger size and weight of a 150Ah battery. It can deliver up to 50 miles per charge, while hills, passenger count, speed, tire size, and driving style will reduce or increase the distance you see in actual use. 
 Can I Charge the ICON Lithium Battery Below Freezing?
 Can I Charge the ICON Lithium Battery Below Freezing?
 Charging automatically stops when battery temperature falls below 32°F and resumes after the battery warms above 41°F. In freezing weather, park the cart in a warmer garage or enclosed space and allow the battery to warm naturally before charging; avoid applying concentrated heat directly to the battery. Because regenerative braking can also return energy to the battery, warming the battery before driving is the better approach when the cart has been sitting in sub-freezing temperatures.
 How Should I Store the Battery When My ICON Is Not Used for Several Months?
 How Should I Store the Battery When My ICON Is Not Used for Several Months?
 Charge the battery before seasonal storage, turn off unnecessary cart loads, and keep the golf cart in a dry location away from prolonged temperature extremes. Check SOC periodically through the LCD or Bluetooth App instead of leaving accessories drawing power for months. Disconnecting unnecessary parasitic loads helps prevent the battery from being slowly discharged while the cart is parked.

 Vatrer backs this battery with a 10-year warranty, giving you long-term coverage after moving away from an aging lead-acid battery bank. Keep your purchase information and follow the specified charging and operating conditions so warranty support can be handled efficiently if a covered battery issue occurs during the warranty period.

 FAQs
 How Far Can a 48V 105Ah Lithium Battery Go on a Full Charge?
 How Far Can a 48V 105Ah Lithium Battery Go on a Full Charge?
 Our 48V 105Ah lithium battery stores 5.376kWh of energy and can deliver up to 50 miles per charge. Actual range changes with terrain, passenger weight, tire size, driving speed, temperature, and accessory use, so we recommend checking the remaining SOC on the LCD display or Vatrer app before a longer route.
 How Long Does It Take To Charge a 48V 105Ah Lithium Golf Cart Battery?
 How Long Does It Take To Charge a 48V 105Ah Lithium Golf Cart Battery?
 With our included 58.4V 18A LiFePO4 charger, the battery can recharge from 0% to 100% in approximately six hours. If charging does not begin, we recommend confirming that the CHG function is on, the connections are secure, the battery is warm enough to accept a charge, and the dedicated lithium battery charger is being used.
 How Often Should i Charge My Lithium Golf Cart Battery?
 How Often Should i Charge My Lithium Golf Cart Battery?
 We recommend recharging when SOC reaches around 20%–30%; you do not need to drain the battery to 0% first. Partial charging works well for shorter daily trips, while charging to 100% gives you more range before a full day on the course or around the neighborhood.
 Can i Charge a Lithium Golf Cart Battery Below Freezing?
 Can i Charge a Lithium Golf Cart Battery Below Freezing?
 Our BMS automatically stops charging when the battery temperature falls below 32°F and allows charging to resume after it rises above 41°F. Move the cart into a warmer garage or enclosed space and allow the battery to warm naturally before reconnecting the charger; do not bypass the low-temperature protection to force a charge.
 Can i Drive My Golf Cart In Freezing Temperatures?
 Can i Drive My Golf Cart In Freezing Temperatures?
 Our battery can discharge at temperatures down to -4°F, but the BMS stops discharge below that point to protect the cells. Cold weather can also temporarily reduce available range, so we recommend starting with a higher SOC, storing the cart indoors when possible, and leaving additional range margin for winter trips.
 Why Does My Lithium Golf Cart Battery Shut Off on Hills?
 Why Does My Lithium Golf Cart Battery Shut Off on Hills?
 A shutdown during a steep climb or hard acceleration may mean the BMS detected excessive current, low voltage, or high temperature and temporarily cut output to protect the battery. Stop safely, release the accelerator, turn off unnecessary accessories, let the battery recover, and check SOC, current, temperature, and fault information on the LCD display or Vatrer app; contact Vatrer support if the same protection event keeps returning.
 Can i Leave My Lithium Golf Cart Battery Plugged In Overnight?
 Can i Leave My Lithium Golf Cart Battery Plugged In Overnight?
 An overnight charge is practical because the included charger normally completes a full 0%–100% cycle in about five hours. We recommend disconnecting the charger after the normal charging cycle rather than leaving the battery on continuous float charge for days or weeks, especially when the cart will not be used.
 How Should i Store a 48V Lithium Golf Cart Battery For Winter?
 How Should i Store a 48V Lithium Golf Cart Battery For Winter?
 For off-season storage, we recommend keeping the battery at approximately 40%–60% SOC, turning off the main power, and disconnecting accessories or other parasitic loads. Check the battery every two to three months, recharge it before SOC falls below 30%, and choose a dry location around 50°F–77°F when available.
 Can a Lithium Golf Cart Battery Get Wet?
 Can a Lithium Golf Cart Battery Get Wet?
 Our battery carries an IP67 rating, which adds protection against dust and temporary water exposure, but the battery system should not be treated as suitable for prolonged submersion or pressure washing. Keep the charger and electrical connections dry, and if water enters the battery compartment, turn the system off and allow the terminals and cables to dry completely before charging or driving again.
 Do Lithium Golf Cart Batteries Require Maintenance?
 Do Lithium Golf Cart Batteries Require Maintenance?
 Our single-battery LiFePO4 system requires no water refilling or acid cleanup. We still recommend occasionally checking terminal tightness, mounting brackets, cable wear, compartment cleanliness, and battery status through the LCD display or Vatrer app so small connection or temperature issues can be handled before they interrupt a ride.

 FAQs
 Will This Narrow Lithium Golf Cart Battery Fit My 48V Cart?
 Will This Narrow Lithium Golf Cart Battery Fit My 48V Cart?
 Yes. We designed this narrow lithium golf cart battery for 48V systems used in Club Car, EZGO, Yamaha, and other 48V golf carts. Its 9.76-inch narrow width is especially useful in long or tight battery compartments where wider 105Ah batteries take up more lateral space.
 If your cart also powers lights, a horn, USB ports, or other 12V accessories, those accessories should run through the cart’s existing 48V-to-12V converter or a dedicated converter after the lithium upgrade.
 Can I Use My Old Lead-Acid Charger With This 48V Lithium Golf Cart Battery?
 Can I Use My Old Lead-Acid Charger With This 48V Lithium Golf Cart Battery?
 Use the included 58.4V 18A LiFePO4 battery charger instead of the charger from your old lead-acid battery. We match this charger to the battery’s charging requirements, so the correct charging solution is already included with your conversion setup.
 After switching to lithium, use the dedicated LiFePO4 battery charger rather than the charging profile designed for your previous lead-acid batteries.
 What Should I Do If the Battery Is Too Cold to Charge?
 What Should I Do If the Battery Is Too Cold to Charge?
 When the battery temperature drops below 23°F, the BMS stops charging to protect the battery cells. Charging automatically becomes available again once the battery warms above 32°F.
 Move the cart into a garage or another enclosed space above freezing and let the battery warm naturally before charging. In areas with frequent freezing temperatures, keeping your charging location above 32°F is the simplest way to maintain normal winter charging.
 Can I Drive a 48V LiFePO4 Golf Cart Battery in Freezing Weather?
 Can I Drive a 48V LiFePO4 Golf Cart Battery in Freezing Weather?
 Yes. This 48V LiFePO4 golf cart battery can continue supplying power in cold weather until low-temperature discharge protection activates below -4°F.
 Cold temperatures can temporarily reduce available range, so begin winter trips with a higher SOC and leave more reserve than you normally would in warm weather. After driving in freezing conditions, let the battery warm above freezing before starting the next charge.
 How Should I Store the Lithium Golf Cart Battery Over Winter?
 How Should I Store the Lithium Golf Cart Battery Over Winter?
 Turn the battery off, disconnect loads that could create a slow parasitic drain, and store the cart or battery in a dry, protected location. For extended storage, keep the SOC above 30% and check it at least once every three months, recharging when necessary.
 Avoid leaving the battery deeply discharged for an entire season. The LCD display or Bluetooth app makes periodic SOC checks quick and easy.
 How Far Will a 48V 105Ah Lithium Golf Cart Battery Go on Hills?
 How Far Will a 48V 105Ah Lithium Golf Cart Battery Go on Hills?
 This 48V 105Ah lithium golf cart battery can provide up to 50 miles per charge. Repeated climbing uses more energy than driving on flat ground, while passenger weight, larger tires, higher speeds, accessories, and frequent acceleration can also reduce total driving distance.
 On hilly routes or with a full passenger load, use the LCD or Bluetooth SOC reading to manage your remaining range. Keeping a comfortable energy reserve before a longer return trip gives you more flexibility throughout the day.
 Will the 200A BMS Handle Steep Hills and Heavy Loads?
 Will the 200A BMS Handle Steep Hills and Heavy Loads?
 The 200A continuous BMS is designed to support the higher current demand created by acceleration, hills, and passenger loads. It also supports short-duration higher current when the cart needs extra power during demanding moments.
 If you have a heavily modified golf cart with a motor and controller setup that requires more than 200A of continuous battery output, the Vatrer 48V 105Ah UTV lithium battery with 300A BMS is the better choice for the higher continuous-current demand.
 Do I Need a 48V to 12V Converter After a Lithium Conversion?
 Do I Need a 48V to 12V Converter After a Lithium Conversion?
 If your cart already uses a 48V-to-12V converter for headlights, turn signals, a horn, radio, or USB ports, you can continue powering those accessories through the converter.
 If your old lead-acid setup powered 12V accessories by tapping only part of the multi-battery bank, add a 48V-to-12V converter when completing the lithium conversion. Do not connect 12V accessories directly to the full 48V lithium battery output.
 When Should I Recharge the Lithium Golf Cart Battery Conversion Kit?
 When Should I Recharge the Lithium Golf Cart Battery Conversion Kit?
 You do not need to discharge LiFePO4 to 0% before charging. For everyday driving, recharging around 20%–30% SOC leaves a useful reserve and keeps the battery from sitting deeply discharged.
 Charge to full before a long golf day, extended neighborhood drive, or other trip where you want maximum available range. Once charging is complete, you can disconnect the charger instead of maintaining the continuous trickle-charging routine commonly associated with flooded lead-acid batteries.
 Can This IP67 Golf Cart Battery Handle Rain and Washing?
 Can This IP67 Golf Cart Battery Handle Rain and Washing?
 Yes. The IP67-rated enclosure helps protect the battery against dust and water exposure encountered during normal outdoor golf cart use, including wet roads, splashes, and rainy conditions.
 Keep terminals and external electrical connections properly secured, avoid directing high-pressure water at connectors, and do not intentionally submerge the battery.

 Will This Narrow Lithium Golf Cart Battery Fit My 48V Cart?
 Will This Narrow Lithium Golf Cart Battery Fit My 48V Cart?
 Yes. We designed this narrow lithium golf cart battery for 48V systems used in Club Car, EZGO, Yamaha, and other 48V golf carts. Its 9.76-inch narrow width is especially useful in long or tight battery compartments where wider 105Ah batteries take up more lateral space.
 If your cart also powers lights, a horn, USB ports, or other 12V accessories, those accessories should run through the cart’s existing 48V-to-12V converter or a dedicated converter after the lithium upgrade.
 Can I Use My Old Lead-Acid Charger With This 48V Lithium Golf Cart Battery?
 Can I Use My Old Lead-Acid Charger With This 48V Lithium Golf Cart Battery?
 Use the included 58.4V 18A LiFePO4 battery charger instead of the charger from your old lead-acid battery. We match this charger to the battery’s charging requirements, so the correct charging solution is already included with your conversion setup.
 After switching to lithium, use the dedicated LiFePO4 battery charger rather than the charging profile designed for your previous lead-acid batteries.
 What Should I Do If the Battery Is Too Cold to Charge?
 What Should I Do If the Battery Is Too Cold to Charge?
 When the battery temperature drops below 23°F, the BMS stops charging to protect the battery cells. Charging automatically becomes available again once the battery warms above 32°F.
 Move the cart into a garage or another enclosed space above freezing and let the battery warm naturally before charging. In areas with frequent freezing temperatures, keeping your charging location above 32°F is the simplest way to maintain normal winter charging.
 Can I Drive a 48V LiFePO4 Golf Cart Battery in Freezing Weather?
 Can I Drive a 48V LiFePO4 Golf Cart Battery in Freezing Weather?
 Yes. This 48V LiFePO4 golf cart battery can continue supplying power in cold weather until low-temperature discharge protection activates below -4°F.
 Cold temperatures can temporarily reduce available range, so begin winter trips with a higher SOC and leave more reserve than you normally would in warm weather. After driving in freezing conditions, let the battery warm above freezing before starting the next charge.
 How Should I Store the Lithium Golf Cart Battery Over Winter?
 How Should I Store the Lithium Golf Cart Battery Over Winter?
 Turn the battery off, disconnect loads that could create a slow parasitic drain, and store the cart or battery in a dry, protected location. For extended storage, keep the SOC above 30% and check it at least once every three months, recharging when necessary.
 Avoid leaving the battery deeply discharged for an entire season. The LCD display or Bluetooth app makes periodic SOC checks quick and easy.
 How Far Will a 48V 105Ah Lithium Golf Cart Battery Go on Hills?
 How Far Will a 48V 105Ah Lithium Golf Cart Battery Go on Hills?
 This 48V 105Ah lithium golf cart battery can provide up to 50 miles per charge. Repeated climbing uses more energy than driving on flat ground, while passenger weight, larger tires, higher speeds, accessories, and frequent acceleration can also reduce total driving distance.
 On hilly routes or with a full passenger load, use the LCD or Bluetooth SOC reading to manage your remaining range. Keeping a comfortable energy reserve before a longer return trip gives you more flexibility throughout the day.
 Will the 200A BMS Handle Steep Hills and Heavy Loads?
 Will the 200A BMS Handle Steep Hills and Heavy Loads?
 The 200A continuous BMS is designed to support the higher current demand created by acceleration, hills, and passenger loads. It also supports short-duration higher current when the cart needs extra power during demanding moments.
 If you have a heavily modified golf cart with a motor and controller setup that requires more than 200A of continuous battery output, the Vatrer 48V 105Ah UTV lithium battery with 300A BMS is the better choice for the higher continuous-current demand.
 Do I Need a 48V to 12V Converter After a Lithium Conversion?
 Do I Need a 48V to 12V Converter After a Lithium Conversion?
 If your cart already uses a 48V-to-12V converter for headlights, turn signals, a horn, radio, or USB ports, you can continue powering those accessories through the converter.
 If your old lead-acid setup powered 12V accessories by tapping only part of the multi-battery bank, add a 48V-to-12V converter when completing the lithium conversion. Do not connect 12V accessories directly to the full 48V lithium battery output.
 When Should I Recharge the Lithium Golf Cart Battery Conversion Kit?
 When Should I Recharge the Lithium Golf Cart Battery Conversion Kit?
 You do not need to discharge LiFePO4 to 0% before charging. For everyday driving, recharging around 20%–30% SOC leaves a useful reserve and keeps the battery from sitting deeply discharged.
 Charge to full before a long golf day, extended neighborhood drive, or other trip where you want maximum available range. Once charging is complete, you can disconnect the charger instead of maintaining the continuous trickle-charging routine commonly associated with flooded lead-acid batteries.

 Yes. The IP67-rated enclosure helps protect the battery against dust and water exposure encountered during normal outdoor golf cart use, including wet roads, splashes, and rainy conditions.
 Keep terminals and external electrical connections properly secured, avoid directing high-pressure water at connectors, and do not intentionally submerge the battery.
